QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_2

question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (Cat III AIF) is structured as a 'Large Value Fund' where each investor must commit a minimum amount to qualify for the IC-accountability waiver under SEBI (AIF) Regulations. If the fund has 12 investors, each committing exactly the regulatory minimum with the prescribed IC-waiver furnished, what is the minimum total commitment under this waiver carve-out?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the IC member-accountability provision is NOT applicable where each relevant investor has committed minimum INR 70 crore (or equivalent) AND furnished the prescribed waiver. So 12 investors x INR 70 cr = INR 840 cr minimum. The Trap: INR 10 cr is the Cat III SPONSOR commit floor, not the investor-IC-waiver threshold. INR 25 cr is a concentration-limit figure. INR 5 cr is the Cat I/II sponsor minimum — an exam trap swapping categories. Note: Page 277 of the workbook sets the INR 70 crore per-investor waiver carve-out for the IC member-accountability provision.
